games.title: Language Choice
games.description: Choose the form that makes the unit language accurate.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses the Present Simple correctly?
choices: The engineer designing bridges every single day.
rounds.answer: The engineer designs bridges.
rounds.explanation: The subject is he or she, so the verb takes the -s ending and stands alone without an -ing form.

rounds.prompt: Complete the rule with the right modal verb: You _____ ignore someone who needs help.
rounds.answer: mustn't
rounds.explanation: This is a rule about what is not allowed, so mustn't is stronger and more suitable than the advice word should.

rounds.prompt: Which word shows direction in this sentence: The class walked _____ the centre of town?
rounds.answer: towards
rounds.explanation: Towards points the walk at a destination, while in, on and near would hold the class in one place.

games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: Which two workers does the text place in the market, and what does each one do?
choices: The merchant sells fresh fruit and the carpenter mends a wooden stall.
They left because their home was not safe.
She says you mustn't build in a hurry and you should plan carefully and check twice.
rounds.answer: The merchant sells fresh fruit and the carpenter mends a wooden stall.
rounds.explanation: Both workers appear in the market sentence, so the answer names them in the order the text gives.

rounds.prompt: What did Omar come to our town to do?
choices: They left because their home was not safe.
The school was chosen to make posters about the important jobs in their community.
He came to open a market stall and build a better life.
rounds.answer: He came to open a market stall and build a better life.
rounds.explanation: Omar is named as the immigrant, and his two reasons sit side by side in one sentence.

rounds.prompt: What advice does Elena give using should and mustn't?
choices: He made one for the military because they protect us, and one for the refugees who moved here.
She says you mustn't build in a hurry and you should plan carefully and check twice.
He came to open a market stall and build a better life.
rounds.answer: She says you mustn't build in a hurry and you should plan carefully and check twice.
rounds.explanation: The rule and the advice sit in one of her replies, one telling us what is banned and one what is wise.

games.title: Unit Mission
games.description: Finish with a mixed challenge across the whole unit.

rounds.prompt: What does the word 'caretaker' mean?
choices: A person who cleans and takes care of a building.
A machine that lifts heavy stones onto a lorry at a building site.
A short piece of writing printed in a newspaper.
A room where the pupils hang their coats.
rounds.answer: A person who cleans and takes care of a building.
rounds.explanation: In the parade, the caretaker walks proudly in his clean uniform after keeping the school tidy all week.

rounds.prompt: Which meaning matches the word 'senator'?
choices: A person who takes pictures with a camera.
A cart full of fruit that is pushed slowly through the busy market.
A person chosen to help make the laws for a country.
The group of people trained to protect a country.
rounds.answer: A person chosen to help make the laws for a country.
rounds.explanation: A senator works on the laws of a whole country, which is why the newspaper reports the school visit.

rounds.prompt: In this unit, what is an article?
choices: A person who repairs the wooden stalls at the busy market.
A short piece of writing in a newspaper or magazine.
A rule that everyone in the town must obey.
A small bell fixed to the front of a bicycle.
rounds.answer: A short piece of writing in a newspaper or magazine.
rounds.explanation: The messenger's newspaper carries the article about the senator, so an article is writing, not a person.
